candidates.name: PHP array/list destructuring
candidates.proposed_use: Prepare separate optional-value positions from a zero-based heterogeneous PHP array, retaining order, ignoring unused trailing positions and producing null for missing keys.

citations.section: Array destructuring L472–555, especially L502 and L551

candidates.remaining_adapter: Connect the prepared values to the Go caller or implement Go syntax/type integration; caller-specific numeric/type processing remains. The core extraction/null behavior is supplied in the PHP language context.
limitations: PHP list is explicitly named in the frozen first text.
Missing keys emit a warning/notice; no runtime experiment.
Different language and unverified cross-language integration.

candidates.name: JavaScript array destructuring with explicit null defaults
candidates.proposed_use: Use a fixed-width array pattern whose bindings have null default expressions, such as [a=null,b=null,c=null], to take ordered optional values and let the language fill absent positions.

citations.section: Default value L332–349; array assignments/missing elements L376–400; ignoring values L437–453; iterable stopping L518–552

candidates.remaining_adapter: Bridge the prepared values into Go bindings and preserve the intended heterogeneous input domain. Configuring built-in defaults supplies the proposed missing-value policy; no handwritten indexing/padding loop is suggested.
limitations: The null-default pattern is an inference combining delivered rules; not a directly returned exact example or tested runtime result.
Unconfigured destructuring yields undefined, which is not the frozen null/nil output.
No Go compiler integration was examined.
